# package eds

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/eds"
```

Package eds reads, validates and writes CANopen electronic data sheets (EDS) and device configuration files (DCF) as CiA 306-1 specifies them, and converts them to and from an [od.Dictionary](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/od#Dictionary).

#### Model {#hdr-Model}

[Parse](#func-parse) keeps the whole file. The standard sections ([FileInfo](#type-fileinfo), [DeviceInfo](#type-deviceinfo), [DeviceComissioning](#type-devicecomissioning), [DummyUsage](#type-dummyusage), [Comments](#type-comments), the three object lists) and the object sections (\[XXXX], \[XXXXsubY], \[XXXXName], \[XXXXValue], \[XXXXDenotation], \[XXXXObjectLinks]) are interpreted into typed fields; every other section (tools sections, modular-device sections, vendor extensions) is kept verbatim in [File.Unknown](#func-file-unknown), and every key a section does not define, or whose value does not parse as the key's type, is kept verbatim in the section's Extra list. Value literals whose meaning depends on the data type (DefaultValue, LowLimit, HighLimit, ParameterValue) are kept as raw strings and evaluated only when a dictionary is built.

Key and section names are case-insensitive. Lines may end in CRLF or LF, a UTF-8 byte order mark is skipped, lines whose first non-blank character is ';' are comments, and integers are decimal, 0x hexadecimal or octal with a leading 0. Text is kept as the bytes of the file (EDS files from Windows tools are often Latin-1).

Parse fails only on lines it cannot read (a key outside a section, a line that is neither a section header, a key=value pair nor a comment). Everything else, from a missing mandatory object to a default value that does not fit its type, is reported by [File.Validate](#func-file-validate).

#### Round trip {#hdr-Round_trip}

[Write](#func-write) writes the model in a canonical, deterministic layout. Parsing what Write wrote gives the same model, so parse, write and parse again loses no information the model holds. Comments, blank lines, key order inside standard sections, the spelling of numbers and duplicate keys (the last one wins) are not kept.

#### Dictionaries {#hdr-Dictionaries}

[File.Dictionary](#func-file-dictionary) builds an [od.Dictionary](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/od#Dictionary) from the object sections, using ParameterValue when present (DCF) and DefaultValue otherwise. A "$NODEID+offset" value becomes a node-ID-relative default ([od.Variable.NodeIDRelative](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/od#Variable.NodeIDRelative) with the offset as Default), so the dictionary evaluates it for its node-ID and re-evaluates it after [od.Dictionary.SetNodeID](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen/od#Dictionary.SetNodeID) and a reset. [FromDictionary](#func-fromdictionary) goes the other way, for exporting the description or the current configuration of a node.

## Constants

```go
const (
	CompactSub0Name = "NrOfObjects"
)
```

Compact storage names (CiA 306 4.5.2.3): sub-index 0 of an ARRAY with CompactSubObj, and the name pattern of its elements when the object has no \[XXXXName] entry for them (the convention of python canopen: ParameterName, '\_', sub-index in lower-case hexadecimal).

```go
const StringLengthMinKey = "StringLengthMin"
```

StringLengthMinKey is the CANopenNode key giving the allocated length of a string or DOMAIN; [File.BuildDictionary](#func-file-builddictionary) takes it as MaxSize and [FromDictionary](#func-fromdictionary) writes MaxSize to it.

## Functions

### func FormatLiteral

```go
func FormatLiteral(t canopen.DataType, b []byte, nodeRelative bool) string
```

FormatLiteral formats an encoded value of type t as an EDS value literal that [canopen.ParseValue](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-canopen#ParseValue) reads back to the same bytes: unsigned integers in 0x hexadecimal, signed integers in decimal, floats in the shortest decimal form (NaNs as their 0x bit pattern), BOOLEAN as 0/1, VISIBLE\_STRING and UNICODE\_STRING as text, OCTET\_STRING, DOMAIN and the TIME types as hexadecimal digits. With nodeRelative the value is an offset written as "$NODEID+0x...".

### func HasErrors

```go
func HasErrors(ds []Diagnostic) bool
```

HasErrors reports whether any diagnostic is an Error.

### func Write

```go
func Write(w io.Writer, f *File) error
```

Write writes f, an EDS or a DCF (a DCF differs only by its [DeviceComissioning](#type-devicecomissioning) section and ParameterValue keys), in a canonical layout: [FileInfo](#type-fileinfo), [DeviceInfo](#type-deviceinfo), [DeviceComissioning](#type-devicecomissioning), [DummyUsage](#type-dummyusage), [Comments](#type-comments), then each object list followed by its objects, the objects no list names, and the unknown sections. Objects are written in index order, each with its \[XXXXName], \[XXXXValue], \[XXXXDenotation], sub-object and \[XXXXObjectLinks] sections. Lines end in LF.

Write fails when a key or value cannot be written so that Parse reads it back: a line break in a value, an empty or malformed key or section name, an unknown section with a standard name, or an access type out of range. Leading and trailing blanks of values are not kept (Parse trims them).

#### func FromDictionary

```go
func FromDictionary(d *od.Dictionary, opts ExportOptions) *File
```

FromDictionary describes a dictionary as an EDS, or as a DCF holding its current values, for exporting a node's description or configuration. Every object is written expanded (no compact storage); node-ID-relative defaults are written as "$NODEID+0x..."; MaxSize goes to StringLengthMin. The object lists are built with [File.UpdateObjectLists](#func-file-updateobjectlists).

#### func (File) BuildDictionary

```go
func (f *File) BuildDictionary(node canopen.NodeID, opts BuildOptions) (*od.Dictionary, []Diagnostic, error)
```

BuildDictionary builds an object dictionary for a node.

  - The value of a sub-object is its ParameterValue when present (DCF), else its DefaultValue; an empty value is zero (empty for strings).
  - A value with $NODEID ("$NODEID+0x180", "0x180+$NODEID") becomes a node-ID-relative default: Default holds the offset and NodeIDRelative is set, so the dictionary adds its node-ID, now and after SetNodeID and a reset (an LSS node-ID change). $NODEID in a limit is evaluated with node.
  - An ARRAY with CompactSubObj=n is expanded: sub-index 0 (UNSIGNED8, ro, value n, named CompactSub0Name) and sub-indices 1..n with the object's DataType, AccessType, PDOMapping and value, named from \[XXXXName] (or ParameterName\_\<sub>), valued from \[XXXXValue] when present.
  - Objects below 0x1000 (the data type area: DEFTYPE and DEFSTRUCT definitions) and NULL objects are not part of the dictionary and are skipped silently. A variable whose data type is defined that way (or otherwise unknown or structured) cannot be held.
  - A DOMAIN object (or sub-object) without DataType has type DOMAIN. DOMAIN and OCTET\_STRING values are hexadecimal digit pairs.
  - Limits apply to integer and float types and are ignored otherwise.
  - MaxSize of a variable-length value is 0 (unbounded), unless the section has the CANopenNode key StringLengthMin: then it is the larger of that and the length of the value. The length of the default alone is no bound, since writable strings (names, descriptions) commonly default to a shorter text than a device accepts.

In lenient mode the sub-objects that break these rules are skipped (and objects left without sub-objects) and reported as warnings.

#### func (File) SortObjects

```go
func (f *File) SortObjects()
```

SortObjects sorts the objects by index and their sub-objects by sub-index, as Parse leaves them. Call it after adding objects out of order.

#### func (File) UpdateObjectLists

```go
func (f *File) UpdateObjectLists()
```

UpdateObjectLists rebuilds the three object lists from the objects: 0x1000, 0x1001 and 0x1018 are mandatory, 0x2000..0x5FFF manufacturer specific, everything else from 0x1000 up optional.

#### func (File) Validate

```go
func (f *File) Validate() []Diagnostic
```

Validate checks the file against CiA 306 and CiA 301: the mandatory objects 0x1000, 0x1001 and 0x1018; the object lists against the object sections and their declared counts; ObjectType, DataType and AccessType; SubNumber against the sub-object sections and sub-index 0; DefaultValue, ParameterValue and the limits against the data type, and LowLimit ≤ HighLimit; PDOMapping only on mappable types; the PDO objects against NrOfRXPDO and NrOfTXPDO; the compact storage rules; DCF commissioning values; keys whose values do not parse; duplicate keys and sections. A file without Error diagnostics builds a dictionary.
